outcome: Still open as of 10 Oct 2026. Since 26 Jan 2024 two partial lower bounds have appeared, both below the hemisphere value 2π: Briggs and Wells (arXiv 2602.17859, 19 Feb 2026) prove area ≥ (√3/4)π² ≈ 1.3603π for every compact Riemannian isometric filling of the length-2π circle; Chen, Li and Zhong (arXiv 2609.08251, 8 Sep 2026) prove area ≥ 14ζ(3)/π ≈ 5.35677 for all such fillings and > 5.40154 for orientable ones. The Chen–Li–Zhong preprint has a Lean/Mathlib formalisation, a disclosed use of OpenAI language models, and only an automated AI referee so far, which objects to its orientable argument. The disk case (Gromov 1983; Ivanov 2001) and the genus-one case (Bangert, Croke, Ivanov and Katz, 2004) were settled before the window.
problem_asks: (1) Lower bound: for every closed curve of length L that bounds a shortcut-free surface (a surface in which the intrinsic distance between any two boundary points equals their distance measured along the curve), the surface has area at least L²/(2π), the area of the hemisphere whose boundary is a curve of length L. (2) Sharpness: the round hemisphere, which is shortcut-free and has area exactly L²/(2π), attains the bound, so the claim is that the hemisphere is the minimiser. Scope as the frozen wording fixes it: 'shortcut-free surfaces in Euclidean space'. The January 2024 wording says nothing about topology or genus, so the bound is asked for every topological type the statement covers. Two readings of the ambient class differ and are recorded here, not resolved: (a) the current Wikipedia lead, as fetched, says 'orientable surfaces' (the frozen wording may differ; I did not check the Jan 2024 revision); (b) the literature (Gromov 1983 onward) states the conjecture for abstract compact orientable Riemannian surfaces that fill the circle isometrically, not for surfaces embedded in R³. A bound for all abstract Riemannian fillings implies the embedded-class bound, so results in the Riemannian class also bear on the Euclidean wording; the converse does not hold.

events.what_happened: M. Gromov, 'Filling Riemannian manifolds', J. Differential Geom. 18 (1983) 1–147, states the conjecture and proves the disk case: among isometric Riemannian fillings of a circle of length 2π that are homeomorphic to a disk, the round hemisphere has least area. Route per Wikipedia (fetched summary): glue antipodal boundary points to get a projective plane whose systole is π, then apply Pu's isosystolic inequality. A search snippet of the JDG record gives 'received July 30, 1982' (not opened); the first public written argument is taken as the 1983 publication because I found no earlier preprint.
events.delivers: Minimality of the hemisphere (area ≥ L²/(2π)) among isometric Riemannian fillings of the circle whose topology is a disk. Restriction: disk topology only.
events.remains: Every filling of non-disk topology: orientable fillings of genus ≥ 1 and non-orientable fillings, including Euclidean-embedded surfaces of those topologies.

checked_by.who: Journal of Differential Geometry (refereed research journal of record)
checked_by.qualification: Journal publication of the paper; no separate verification statement for the disk argument was found
checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper (1983). No public expert verification of the disk argument was located in the sources I read.

events.directly_checkable: Equality case: the round hemisphere with boundary a great circle of length L has area L²/(2π) and no shortcuts. A flat disk fails the shortcut test (Wikipedia example).
events.direction: Confirms the lower bound L²/(2π) in disk topology, with the hemisphere as the equality case. No counterexample in this class.

events.what_happened: S. V. Ivanov, 'On two-dimensional minimal fillings', Algebra i Analiz 13(1) (2001) 26–38 (Russian); English version St. Petersburg Math. J. 13(1) (2002) 17–25. Per the Wikipedia summary and a search snippet, this gives a second proof of the disk case (hemisphere least among isometric fillings homeomorphic to a disk), not using uniformisation but using how curves on a disk must cross. I opened only the Math-Net/mathdoc metadata record, which has no abstract; the content is from secondary reports and is not verified against the paper.
events.revisions: Russian original 2001; English translation 2002 (St. Petersburg Math. J.).
events.delivers: Per secondary report only: the disk case again by a different argument. Restriction: disk-homeomorphic fillings.

checked_by.who: Algebra i Analiz / St. Petersburg Mathematical Journal (refereed journals)
checked_by.what_they_did: Published (2001 Russian; 2002 English). No specific verification statement found.

events.doubts: Content not read by me. The 2001 vs 2002 date difference is a publication-year difference (Russian original vs English translation), not a dispute about content.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture: confirms the disk case by a second route. No counterexample.

events.what_happened: V. Bangert, C. Croke, S. Ivanov, M. Katz, 'Filling area conjecture and ovalless real hyperelliptic surfaces', arXiv math/0405583 (v1 submitted 30 May 2004; v2 14 Dec 2004, current), to appear in Geom. Funct. Anal. 15(3) (2005) 577–597 (bibliographic details from Briggs–Wells' reference list, which I read). The arXiv abstract as read: establishes the conjecture for all genus-1 fillings of the circle, extending Pu's genus-0 result. Method per abstract: integral-geometric comparison with orbifold metrics of constant positive curvature on real surfaces of even positive genus, with Weierstrass points as the singular points, and combinatorial analysis of closed ovalless curves.
events.revisions: v1 30 May 2004; v2 14 Dec 2004 (current); journal GAFA 15(3) (2005) per Briggs–Wells reference list.
events.delivers: The hemisphere is minimal among orientable genus-1 isometric Riemannian fillings of the circle of length 2π (scaling gives any length). Restriction: genus one only.
events.remains: Orientable genus ≥ 2; non-orientable fillings not covered by the genus-one or disk arguments.

checked_by.who: Geometric and Functional Analysis (refereed journal of record)
checked_by.what_they_did: Published (2005, per the reference list in Briggs–Wells and Chen–Li–Zhong). No specific public verification statement found.

events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture in genus 1. No counterexample.

events.what_happened: D. Burago, S. Ivanov, 'On asymptotic volume of Finsler tori, minimal surfaces in normed spaces, and symplectic filling volume', Annals of Mathematics 156(3) (2002) 891–914. The Wikipedia article (fetched summary) states that the conjecture is false if Finsler 2-chains with rational coefficients are admitted as fillings, citing this paper. The Annals page I opened has no abstract and does not mention the filling of the circle, the hemisphere, rational coefficients or Finsler 2-chains, so I could not verify the claim.
events.delivers: Per Wikipedia only, unverified: the hemisphere bound fails for a different class, Finsler 2-chains with rational coefficients. Restriction: that class; it does not touch Riemannian fillings of the circle.
events.remains: The Riemannian problem as stated in the bullet, which this event does not address.

checked_by.who: Annals of Mathematics (refereed journal of record)
checked_by.what_they_did: Published (2002). No verification of the rational-coefficient claim was found.

events.doubts: Claim not verified: the cited page has no abstract, and I did not open the paper text. If the claim is correct it is a counterexample in a wider class than the bullet, so it would be a discounted analogue.
events.direction: Per Wikipedia, the bound fails for the rational-Finsler-chain class. That is a different class from the bullet's surfaces, so if correct it is a discounted analogue, not a counterexample to the bullet.

events.what_happened: G. R. Chambers, 'On minimal higher genus fillings', arXiv 2202.01342, submitted 3 Feb 2022 (16 pages, 3 figures; one version; no journal reference on the arXiv page). Abstract as read (condensed by the fetch tool): for a genus-G orientable surface M with a single boundary circle and a disc D whose interior points are joined by unique geodesics, with distances in D at least those in M between boundary points, the area of M scaled by (1 + 2G/π) is at least the area of D. A later reference list (secondary, unverified) gives the venue as Journal of Topology and Analysis, published online 9 April 2026.
events.delivers: For orientable genus-G fillings with one boundary circle: area(M) ≥ area(D)/(1 + 2G/π) for a comparison disc D satisfying the stated hypotheses. My reading, not stated in the abstract: taking D as the hemisphere gives area ≥ 2π/(1 + 2G/π) for genus G, which is below 2π for G ≥ 1. The hypotheses for the hemisphere were not checked. Restriction: orientable, one boundary component, genus G.
events.remains: The sharp value 2π for every genus G ≥ 1; the genus-dependent constant falls short of it.
events.doubts: Journal publication (JTA, 2026) reported only by a secondary reference list; not confirmed. Not a verified check of the argument.
events.direction: Genus-dependent lower bound below 2π for higher-genus orientable fillings. Consistent with the conjecture; no counterexample.

events.what_happened: M. Cossarini, 'Discrete surfaces with length and area and minimal fillings of the circle', arXiv 2009.02415, submitted 4 Sep 2020 (one version; arXiv comments label it a PhD thesis). Models Riemannian and self-reverse Finsler metrics as systems of 'walls' whose crossings count length and area; states a discrete filling inequality (a square-celled surface that fills a 2n-cycle isometrically has at least n(n−1)/2 squares); claims this discrete statement is equivalent to the Gromov FAC for self-reverse metric surfaces; claims a second proof of the disk case for self-reverse metrics (via Steinitz's algorithm and adapting Ivanov's argument), and the FAC for Möbius bands with self-reverse metrics; treats Klein bottles (a systolic inequality).
events.delivers: Claimed: (i) equivalence of the discrete filling inequality with the FAC for self-reverse (which include Riemannian) metric surfaces; (ii) a second proof of the disk case for self-reverse metrics; (iii) the FAC for Möbius bands with self-reverse metrics. Restriction: the discrete inequality itself is not established for higher genus in the abstract.
events.remains: The discrete inequality for orientable surfaces of genus ≥ 1, hence the continuous FAC there; the directed (non-reversible) case, which the abstract says is only discretised as triangulations.

checked_by.who: Doctoral committee of the thesis (names not found in the sources)
checked_by.qualification: Approval of a PhD thesis is implied by the PhD designation in the arXiv comments; committee not named

events.time_since_posted: 6 years (Sep 2020); cited by Chen–Li–Zhong (2026) for the equivalence, but I found no independent verification
events.doubts: The equivalence and the disk and Möbius claims rest on the thesis. I found no independent check of the equivalence in any source I read. The Chen–Li–Zhong text, as fetched, reports Cossarini's equivalence as a citation.
events.direction: Reformulation and partial results, consistent with the conjecture. No counterexample.

events.what_happened: O. Müller, 'A local systolic inequality and Gromov's filling area conjecture', arXiv 2009.03172. v1 submitted 7 Sep 2020; v2 submitted 3 Oct 2020 and now withdrawn, with the comment 'Withdrawn due to a computational error in the derivation of the main results'. The abstract as it stands (of the withdrawn version): the paper aimed to show that a filling of the circle with volume below 2π is never attained, and to prove a local systolic inequality giving an a priori lower bound on total volume; it then says the proof of both assertions 'suffered from a computational mistake' and that 'the second of which is wrong'. I did not read the v1 text.
events.delivers: Claimed, not established after withdrawal: no filling of the circle with area below 2π is attained. The local systolic inequality is stated to be wrong. The withdrawal notice does not say which of the two assertions the computational error affects.
events.remains: Everything: no sound argument for the non-attainment claim is present in the record.
events.doubts: Withdrawn for a computational error. The withdrawn version says the local systolic inequality is wrong; it does not clearly say the non-attainment claim is wrong. No later version found.

withdrawn.what: v2 withdrawn with the comment 'Withdrawn due to a computational error in the derivation of the main results'; the abstract states that the local systolic inequality (the second assertion) is wrong
withdrawn.date: 2020-10-03 (v2 submission; the withdrawal is carried by v2)

events.direction: Claimed direction consistent with the conjecture (no filling below 2π attained). Claims no counterexample. Withdrawn.

events.what_happened: R. Züst, 'The Riemannian hemisphere is almost calibrated in the injective hull of its boundary', arXiv 2104.04498. v1 submitted 9 Apr 2021; v2 submitted 17 Sep 2025 (current; 49 pages per arXiv comment; written while the author was at the University of Bern). Constructs an exact two-form in the injective hull of the Riemannian circle whose comass (defined with inscribed Riemannian area on normed planes) is stationary at every point of the open hemisphere. The HTML v2, as read (first 100,000 characters), gives Theorem 1.2 as: for real rectifiable currents S, T in a metric space X, with S an isometric hemisphere, ∂T = ∂S, and T and S agreeing near the boundary, the inscribed Riemannian mass satisfies M_ir(T) ≥ 2π − C·h^ξ, with h the directed Hausdorff distance between supports, for constants C > 0 and ξ in (1, 2) that depend on r in (0, π/2). The abstract phrases it as 'at least 2π plus a second-order term in the Hausdorff distance'. The author remarks that the form does not seem to be a global calibration.
events.revisions: v1 9 Apr 2021; v2 17 Sep 2025 (current). No journal reference on the arXiv page.
events.delivers: A lower bound on the inscribed Riemannian (Finsler-type) mass: area ≥ 2π − C·h^ξ for fillings within Hausdorff distance h of an isometric hemisphere; a liminf ≥ 2π for sequences converging to a hemisphere (Corollary 1.3 as read). Restriction: near the hemisphere only; the bound is for the inscribed Riemannian mass in metric spaces.
events.remains: The global statement: fillings not close to a hemisphere in Hausdorff distance. The author's own remark says the form is not a global calibration.
events.doubts: The sign and form of the correction term differ between the abstract as read ('2π plus a second-order term') and Theorem 1.2 as read ('2π − C·h^ξ'). I did not reconcile these; the theorem statement is what I read in the paper's HTML. A journal version (Calc. Var. PDE 2025) appeared in one search snippet but not on the arXiv page; unverified.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture: a 2π lower bound holds locally, near the hemisphere. No counterexample.

events.what_happened: C. Ambi, 'A Systolic Inequality for the Filling Area Conjecture', arXiv 2301.08503, submitted 20 Jan 2023 (v1 only; 7 pages; math.DG; no journal reference). Abstract as read (paraphrased by the fetch tool): proves an upper bound on the systolic ratio of an orientable isometric filling of the circle by a Riemannian metric, depending only on the genus. Applied to orientable isometric fillings with a certain lower bound on the systole, it yields the Filling Area Conjecture for that class when the genus is sufficiently large.
events.delivers: The conjecture for orientable isometric fillings of the circle that satisfy a systole lower bound, when the genus is sufficiently large. The genus threshold and the systole bound are not stated on the abstract page I read. Restriction: orientable; large genus; systole hypothesis.
events.remains: Genus below the threshold; fillings without the systole hypothesis; the conjecture in general.
events.time_since_posted: 3 years 9 months (Jan 2023); no journal reference or review found
events.doubts: Threshold and systole hypothesis not read. A search summary wrongly attributed the genus-one case to Ambi; the genus-one case is Bangert–Croke–Ivanov–Katz (2004), and the abstract I read concerns large genus.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture in the stated class. No counterexample.

events.what_happened: S. V. Ivanov, 'Filling minimality of Finslerian 2-discs', arXiv 0910.2257 (v1 13 Oct 2009; v2 16 Oct 2009); Proc. Steklov Inst. Math. 273 (2011) 176–190. Abstract as read: a Riemannian metric on the 2-disc all of whose geodesics are minimal is a minimal filling of its boundary among disc-homeomorphic fillings, removing a boundary-convexity assumption from an earlier result; extended to Finsler metrics with Holmes–Thompson area; described as a Finsler generalisation of Pu's isosystolic inequality. The page does not mention the hemisphere.
events.revisions: v1 13 Oct 2009; v2 16 Oct 2009; journal Proc. Steklov Inst. Math. 273 (2011).
events.delivers: Disk case with an extended class: among disc-homeomorphic fillings, a Riemannian or Finsler (Holmes–Thompson area) disc whose geodesics are all minimal is a minimal filling. Whether the round hemisphere satisfies the geodesic hypothesis was not checked from the abstract. Restriction: disc topology.
events.remains: Non-disc topologies. The link to the hemisphere is via Pu's inequality, per secondary reports.

checked_by.who: Proceedings of the Steklov Institute of Mathematics (refereed journal)
checked_by.what_they_did: Published (2011). No specific verification statement found.

events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture in the disk case and its Finsler extension. No counterexample.

events.what_happened: D. Burago, S. Ivanov, 'Boundary rigidity and filling volume minimality of metrics close to a flat one', Annals of Mathematics 171(2) (2010) 1183–1211 (published online 25 Mar 2010). Result as read from the Annals page (condensed): a metric on a region of Euclidean space with connected boundary that is sufficiently C²-close to Euclidean is a minimal orientable filling; the equality case gives boundary rigidity. The page does not mention the hemisphere, positive curvature or the filling area conjecture. The preprint date was not established; the journal year is used.
events.delivers: Filling-volume minimality for metrics near-flat on Euclidean regions. Restriction: near-Euclidean, not positively curved.
events.remains: The round hemisphere, which is far from flat.

checked_by.who: Annals of Mathematics (refereed journal of record)
checked_by.what_they_did: Published (2010). No specific verification statement found.

events.doubts: A search summary claims small spherical caps are minimal fillings by this paper; the Annals abstract as read does not say so. Treated as an analogue, not a case.
events.direction: Analogue for near-flat metrics; no bearing on the round hemisphere beyond supporting evidence. No counterexample.

events.what_happened: J. Briggs and C. Wells (Auburn University), 'A discrete view of Gromov's filling area conjecture', arXiv 2602.17859, v1 submitted 19 Feb 2026 (10 pages, 4 figures; math.DG primary, math.CO). Discrete part: δ-Lipschitz fillings of the n-cycle have |V(K)| ≥ δ³(n−1)²/8 + (n−1)/2 (Thm 2.1, via Menger-type graph arguments). PL metric surfaces: area ≥ (√3/16)δ³ℓ² (Thm 3.3). Riemannian: Thm 1.2, every compact Riemannian surface isometrically filling the Riemannian circle of length 2π has area ≥ (√3/4)π² ≈ 1.3603π (≈ 4.2737), with no orientability assumption. A related talk, 'Gromov's Filling Area Conjecture, Discretized' (Auburn DMS Combinatorics Seminar, 1 Oct 2025), is dated to the write-up, not the talk.
events.delivers: Any compact Riemannian isometric filling of the circle of length 2π, of any topology, has area ≥ (√3/4)π² ≈ 1.3603π. Restriction: the circle of length 2π (scale for other lengths); the discrete results are for the graph model.
events.remains: The gap from 1.3603π to the conjectured 2π, i.e. the conjecture itself; the question whether the discrete problem is equivalent to Gromov's (open per Chen–Li–Zhong's report of the authors).
events.time_since_posted: 7 months (19 Feb to 10 Oct 2026); cited by two later preprints (May and Sep 2026); no published verification of the argument found
events.doubts: No specific error identified. Caveats on the record: the discrete model is a relaxation (He 2026 says so of the discrete problem in general; Chen–Li–Zhong report the authors' open question on equivalence). The transfer to Riemannian surfaces uses a PL approximation (Cheeger–Müller–Schrader, per Corollary 3.4 as read). No human reviewer found.
events.direction: Lower bound 1.3603π, strictly below the hemisphere value 2π. Consistent with the conjecture; no counterexample.

events.what_happened: R. He, 'An Upper Bound for Discrete Isometric Filling of Cycles', arXiv 2605.08909, v1 submitted 9 May 2026 (only version listed; math.DG, cross-listed math.CO). Graph-metric analogue for the cycle C_n: constructs isometric (no-shortcut) triangulated fillings with (1/6 + o(1))n² vertices, giving D* ≤ 1/6, improving the discretised-hemisphere value 1/(π√3) ≈ 0.184. The abstract as read says the discrete problem is a genuine relaxation of Gromov's problem and cannot settle it.
events.delivers: An upper bound on the discrete vertex-count constant for cycle graphs, D* ≤ 1/6. Restriction: a graph model of the cycle; the author says it is a relaxation and does not settle the continuous conjecture.
events.remains: Everything about the continuous hemisphere bound.
events.doubts: Full text not read; only the abstract page and a search snippet of the introduction.
events.direction: Discrete analogue. By the author's own account it does not cut toward or against the continuous conjecture.
events.object: A family of isometric concentric annular triangulated fillings of C_n with (1/6 + o(1))n² vertices (construction described in the abstract; not read in full).

events.what_happened: L. Chen, X. Li, Y. Zhong, 'A Fourier approach to Gromov's filling area conjecture', arXiv 2609.08251, v1 submitted 8 Sep 2026 (single version; math.DG). Claims: Theorem 1.1, every compact connected Riemannian isometric filling of the circle of length 2π, orientable or not, has area ≥ 14ζ(3)/π ≈ 5.35677; Theorem 1.2, every compact connected orientable such filling has area > 5.40154. Method: odd Fourier coefficients of boundary distance functions, combined with orthogonal mixing and a planar coverage argument; for orientable fillings, a cubic resonant perturbation of the Fourier map compared with the change in comass. Theorem 4.1 is also stated. The paper's acknowledgements include an AI disclosure (quoted in ai) and a companion Lean/Mathlib repository, github.com/lowrank/gromov-filling-lower-bound, which I read from its README.
events.delivers: Area ≥ 14ζ(3)/π ≈ 5.35677 for every compact connected Riemannian isometric filling of the length-2π circle, any topology. For orientable fillings, area > 5.40154. Restriction: Riemannian metrics, boundary length 2π (scale for other lengths). Both bounds are strict and below 2π ≈ 6.2832.
events.remains: The sharp value 2π, for orientable fillings and for all fillings; the gap from 5.40154 (or 5.35677) to 2π.

checked_by.who: Pith (AI referee; the page lists the referee model as deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash)
checked_by.what_they_did: AI 'T0' review: an AI read the paper and answered a fixed list of questions, on 9 Sep 2026. Verdict as read: 'Strong new bound for non-orientable fillings; orientable improvement has a clear frequency mismatch in the perturbation.' 2 major and 3 minor objections; the referee concludes the Theorem 1.2 argument 'is not valid as written'. The page states: 'This review was written by an AI. No human expert has reviewed this paper yet.'

events.time_since_posted: about 1 month (posted 8 Sep 2026); no human expert review found

machine_checked.system: Lean 4 with Mathlib v4.29.0 (paper: 'Lean proofs of Theorems 1.1, 1.2, and 4.1, using Lean and Mathlib 4.29.0, are available in the companion repository'; README: mathlib v4.29.0 at commit 8a178386…)
machine_checked.note: Sorry-freedom is inferred from the README: its axiom audit accepts only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound, and the build script 'rejects source-level proof escapes'. The README does not say 'sorry-free' in words. The README says Lean verifies Theorems 1.1 and 1.2 'at stated compact Riemannian isometric-filling interfaces' and that Theorem 1.2 reads 'oriented' through a project-defined orientation structure. CI run 34177156896 passed on tree commit 57500b07…; the paper links commit ca06f373…; I did not reconcile the two commits and did not open the individual .lean files.

events.doubts: (a) The automated referee says the orientable argument in Section 4 has a frequency mismatch (it obtains frequency n+3 where n is needed; the page's editor's note gives n+4) and that Theorem 1.2 'is not valid as written'. No author reply is in the record I read. (b) This conflicts with the README, which says Theorem 1.2 is verified in Lean. The formal statement encodes 'oriented' through a project-defined orientation structure, so whether it matches the paper's argument is not established by what I read. (c) The AI disclosure says OpenAI models were used 'while developing and checking the Fourier and nonlinear-resonance arguments'; the nonlinear-resonance argument is the orientable perturbation at issue in (a). The record does not say which steps the model produced and which it checked. (d) Authorship of the Pith editor's note and extended notes is not stated. (e) The paper's commit link and the CI-checked commit differ (see machine_checked).
events.direction: Lower bounds 5.35677 (all fillings) and 5.40154 (orientable), both strictly below the hemisphere value 2π ≈ 6.2832. Consistent with the conjecture; no counterexample; it improves Briggs–Wells' 1.3603π.

systems.name: OpenAI language models
systems.what_it_did: Per the authors: used 'while developing and checking the Fourier and nonlinear-resonance arguments'. The sentence does not say which steps were generated by the model, which were checked by it, or how much. The paper's Lean formalisation is not attributed to any AI system in the paper's text.
systems.basis_quote: We used OpenAI language models while developing and checking the Fourier and nonlinear-resonance arguments. The authors are responsible for the mathematical content.

events.what_happened: T. Ikonen, D. Marti, N. Vikman, 'Systolic inequalities for metric surfaces via filling minimality', arXiv 2607.22290, v1 submitted 24 Jul 2026 (17 pages; math.MG, cross-listed math.DG; no journal reference). Optimal systolic inequalities for length spaces homeomorphic to a torus or the real projective plane; the RP² case extends 'a minimality result of hemispheres'. The abstract as read does not mention Gromov's filling area conjecture or the 2π problem.
events.delivers: Optimal systolic constants for RP² and torus length spaces, matching the reversible Finsler constants. Not a filling of a circle.
events.remains: The filling area conjecture is untouched.
events.direction: A different question (closed-surface systolic constant), not a filling claim. Recorded as a discounted neighbour.

events.what_happened: J. Bernstein, D. Ketover, 'Minimal equatorial fillings', arXiv 2609.26701, v1 submitted 22 Sep 2026 (457 KB). Shows that a great circle in S³ bounds embedded non-orientable minimal surfaces of unbounded genus, realising all non-zero Euler numbers (answering a question of Hardt and Rosenberg, 1990), and gives the first real-analytic Jordan curve bounding infinitely many embedded minimal surfaces of distinct topological types. The abstract does not mention Gromov's conjecture or the hemisphere.
events.delivers: Minimal surfaces in S³ bounded by a great circle. Not isometric fillings and not area minimisers among shortcut-free surfaces. Discounted: a different question that shares the word 'fillings'.
events.direction: A different question. Does not bear on the hemisphere bound.

disputes.summary: Credit for the disk case. Wikipedia and the arXiv papers credit Gromov (1983), with Pu's isosystolic inequality (1952) as the tool. Grokipedia instead says 'The sharp lower bound of 2π ... was proved later by Pu in 2002' and attributes the genus-one case to four named authors in 2005. Grokipedia's own page says it was 'written and fact-checked by Grok', so I weigh it as unreliable and record the conflict only.

Wikipedia says the conjecture is false if Finsler 2-chains with rational coefficients are admitted as fillings, citing Burago and Ivanov (Annals 2002). Unverified: the cited Annals page has no abstract and I did not read the paper. If correct, the class differs from the bullet's surfaces.

Status of Chen–Li–Zhong Theorem 1.2 (orientable, > 5.40154). The Lean README says Theorem 1.2 is verified; the Pith automated referee says the orientable argument has a frequency mismatch and is 'not valid as written'. Neither conflict is resolved in the sources I read; no human expert review exists yet.

summary: Still open. Two lower-bound preprints fall in the window and both are below 2π. Briggs and Wells (arXiv 2602.17859, Feb 2026, Auburn, human authors, no published review I could find) prove area ≥ (√3/4)π² ≈ 1.3603π for every compact Riemannian isometric filling of the length-2π circle, any topology; this rests on a discrete graph model transferred to the continuum. Chen, Li and Zhong (arXiv 2609.08251, Sep 2026) claim area ≥ 14ζ(3)/π ≈ 5.35677 for all such fillings and > 5.40154 for orientable ones; this is the strongest bound in the window. Its authors disclose that they 'used OpenAI language models while developing and checking the Fourier and nonlinear-resonance arguments' and cite a Lean/Mathlib formalisation of Theorems 1.1, 1.2 and 4.1 (README read; sorry-freedom inferred from its axiom audit). The only automated review (Pith, an AI referee) reports a frequency mismatch in the orientable argument and says Theorem 1.2 is 'not valid as written'; no human expert has reviewed it per that page. Runtai He (arXiv 2605.08909, May 2026) gives a discrete upper bound D* ≤ 1/6 that the author says cannot settle the continuous conjecture. Ikonen–Marti–Vikman (July 2026) and Bernstein–Ketover (Sep 2026) are discounted neighbours on different questions. Before the window: Gromov 1983 (disk case, hemisphere minimal), Ivanov 2001 and 2009/2011 (disk case and Finsler disk case; the 2001 content is secondary-only), Bangert–Croke–Ivanov–Katz (arXiv May 2004; genus one), Burago–Ivanov 2002 (a rational-Finsler-chain counterexample per Wikipedia, unverified) and 2010 (near-flat analogue), Cossarini (Sep 2020; discrete reformulation with self-reverse disk and Möbius cases), Müller (Sep 2020; withdrawn Oct 2020), Züst (Apr 2021; local bound near the hemisphere, with an abstract-versus-theorem sign discrepancy I did not reconcile), Chambers (Feb 2022; genus-dependent bound below 2π) and Ambi (Jan 2023; large genus with a systole hypothesis). No event claims a counterexample. Close calls for the later pass: (i) whether the Briggs–Wells and Chen–Li–Zhong bounds 'move a quantity the problem names' (the minimal area, which they do) or only give partial information about it (which they do, since neither reaches 2π); (ii) whether the AI disclosure is load-bearing, since 'developing' the nonlinear-resonance argument may describe a contribution to the mathematics, while 'checking' does not; the record does not say which; (iii) how much weight the Lean verification carries against the automated referee's objection to the same orientable step, given the formal statement encodes orientation through a project-defined structure. The Wikipedia lead, as fetched, says 'orientable surfaces', while the frozen statement says 'surfaces in Euclidean space'; I did not check the January 2024 revision. AI involvement: the only system named in any source I read is 'OpenAI language models' (Chen–Li–Zhong), credited in the authors' own words; no named model appears. A lead I could not confirm: the Lean repository contains an AGENTS.md described as a 'repository contract for coding agents' (the README lists it), which would suggest a coding agent in the formalisation, but the file returned HTTP 503 twice, so I attribute nothing to it. An OpenAI August 2026 'Ten advances in mathematics and theoretical computer science' post was checked only through secondary coverage (the primary page returned 403); the listed results were geometry, coding theory, group theory, operator algebras, complexity, cryptography and combinatorics, and none is reported as concerning filling areas, so I record it as a dead end, not a finding.
competing_reading: Read Chen–Li–Zhong as the strongest recent movement on the minimal-area quantity: it improves the constant of the Briggs–Wells bound from about 4.27 to about 5.40 for orientable fillings, and a formal Lean verification exists for the stated theorems. On that reading the event counts as machine-checked progress that moves the named quantity, with the AI disclosure a credited contribution to the Fourier arguments. The opposite reading: the orientable step (Theorem 1.2) has an automated referee's unanswered frequency objection; the Lean formal statement encodes 'oriented' through a project-defined structure, so the Lean check may not be a check of the paper's argument; and the only human-facing status is 'no human expert has reviewed this'. On that reading the orientable bound is unestablished, and the general bound (5.35677) rests on the same Fourier method. A reading that discounts all the 2026 bounds would say none of them is a bound on the problem as asked (the 2π claim), so none moves the problem's status, only its partial values.
what_would_settle_it: (1) The full text of arXiv 2609.08251, Section 4 and the acknowledgements, verified verbatim against the PDF (the PDF fetch returned binary; I read the HTML through a summariser), together with an answer to the frequency objection (n+3 against n, and the editor's n+4). (2) The Lean formal statement of Theorem 1.2 and its orientation structure, set against the paper's definition of orientable filling. (3) The repository's AGENTS.md and commit history, to learn who wrote the Lean code and whether a coding agent did. (4) Any human expert verification or refereeing of either 2026 preprint. (5) The OpenAI primary 'Ten advances' post (403 here), to confirm no filling-area result is listed. (6) The text of Ivanov's 2001 paper, to confirm the disk-case content I took from secondary reports. (7) The January 2024 revision of the Wikipedia article, and the primary Burago–Ivanov 2002 statement on rational Finsler chains. (8) The Züst theorem's sign: whether the bound is 2π − C·h^ξ or 2π plus a second-order term.

event.what_happened: J. Briggs and C. Wells (Auburn University), 'A discrete view of Gromov's filling area conjecture', arXiv 2602.17859, v1 submitted 19 Feb 2026 (10 pages, 4 figures; math.DG primary, math.CO). Discrete part: δ-Lipschitz fillings of the n-cycle have |V(K)| ≥ δ³(n−1)²/8 + (n−1)/2 (Thm 2.1, via Menger-type graph arguments). PL metric surfaces: area ≥ (√3/16)δ³ℓ² (Thm 3.3). Riemannian: Thm 1.2, every compact Riemannian surface isometrically filling the Riemannian circle of length 2π has area ≥ (√3/4)π² ≈ 1.3603π (≈ 4.2737), with no orientability assumption. A related talk, 'Gromov's Filling Area Conjecture, Discretized' (Auburn DMS Combinatorics Seminar, 1 Oct 2025), is dated to the write-up, not the talk.
event.delivers: Any compact Riemannian isometric filling of the circle of length 2π, of any topology, has area ≥ (√3/4)π² ≈ 1.3603π. Restriction: the circle of length 2π (scale for other lengths); the discrete results are for the graph model.
event.remains: The gap from 1.3603π to the conjectured 2π, i.e. the conjecture itself; the question whether the discrete problem is equivalent to Gromov's (open per Chen–Li–Zhong's report of the authors).
event.time_since_posted: 7 months (19 Feb to 10 Oct 2026); cited by two later preprints (May and Sep 2026); no published verification of the argument found
event.doubts: No specific error identified. Caveats on the record: the discrete model is a relaxation (He 2026 says so of the discrete problem in general; Chen–Li–Zhong report the authors' open question on equivalence). The transfer to Riemannian surfaces uses a PL approximation (Cheeger–Müller–Schrader, per Corollary 3.4 as read). No human reviewer found.
event.direction: Lower bound 1.3603π, strictly below the hemisphere value 2π. Consistent with the conjecture; no counterexample.

judgement.why: The statement asks for the minimal area (hemisphere) over all shortcut-free fillings of any topology, so the disk, genus-one, Möbius (self-reverse) and large-genus-with-systole results are cases, and the topology-free lower bounds of Briggs–Wells (≈1.36π) and Chen–Li–Zhong (≈5.357, >5.40 orientable) are bounds on the minimal area that stay below 2π. Chambers's genus-dependent constant is likewise a bound. Züst's local result concerns inscribed Riemannian mass of currents in metric spaces near a hemisphere, a changed question, so variant; the discrete, near-flat, rational-Finsler, closed-surface systolic and minimal-surface-in-S³ events are variants. Müller is withdrawn. Chen–Li–Zhong stays credible: the only objection to its orientable step comes from an AI referee (F8), the Lean build is not digestion (F7), and Theorem 1.1 carries no specific objection. The close call is its AI role: 'used OpenAI language models while developing and checking the Fourier and nonlinear-resonance arguments' does not say that the model produced any argument, construction or case in the result, and 'the authors are responsible for the mathematical content' points the other way, so I answered none rather than assisted.
judgement.doubts: Chen–Li–Zhong's AI role could be assisted if 'developing' meant the model supplied parts of the nonlinear-resonance argument; the record cannot settle this. Pith's unanswered frequency-mismatch objection to Theorem 1.2 was automated and is not a knock-down, but a human should check it; the general bound in Theorem 1.1 would survive regardless. Cossarini's thesis committee is unnamed, so I left it unreviewed. Ambi's genus threshold and systole hypothesis were never read. The frozen wording ('surfaces in Euclidean space') differs from the Riemannian-filling literature; the scopes above hold under either reading.
